high.candidate: Breakthrough Listen L band (2.9 Hz channels, 300 s, 0.01 Hz/s), whose archive API returns 404 from this workspace
high.requirement: a fine-channel dataset near 1.4 GHz, at least one decade above the low band

decision_rule: p within 5% of 1.0000 keeps the flat-rung-rate statement and refutes the pitch; p within 5% of 0.3063 keeps the pitch and refutes the flat rung rate; neither means both are refuted by these data.
evidence_required: two bands at least one decade apart
at least three resolved drifting lines in each band
drifts measured in the same unit and the same reference frame

golden_axis.note: no reachable archive band sits on an integer rung offset; the registered prediction is evaluated at the offset the data actually have, and the deficit is recorded rather than absorbed
golden_axis.ratio_definition: high band drift over low band drift
golden_axis.use: the axis fixes the band separation, so the predicted drift ratio between the bands is a pure power of phi

note: the statistic, the predictions and the decision rule are unchanged; only the band that cannot carry them is replaced, and the reason is recorded with its arithmetic

golden_axis.statement: the golden axis read as a log-log slope: the rung rate falls 4.94x per decade

statistic: p = d ln|drift| / d ln f over confirmed drifting lines
test: rung rate versus frequency, two bands

arithmetic.conclusion: the channel width is the limit, not the cadence
